Messages.Author: Dasein
Messages.Body:
Well in this new set we have another instance of a "mystery" keyword:
the event Hunger Moon is labelled "Transient". As far as I know, the
only other cards with this keyword are Waiting Game and White Nights
Massacre. Does anyone have any idea what this might mean? (yes I
realise that at the moment, Transient means nothing since there are no
cards or rules that refer to Transient cards, but I was wondering if
anyone had any clues or speculation? something relating to a
storyline, or obscure WoD lore, or anything?)

There are some other mystery keywords too. Didn't the Port Authority
promo card have the keyword Government? Along with I think NSA Trio
and maybe something else? And I believe the card Inconnu Tutelage has
the Inconnu keyword, and is all on its ownsome lonesome :(

The one thing tying all these cards together is that they are all
events, and there is already a big set of events that have another
important keyword: Gehenna, and there are many, many cards and effects
that refer to Gehenna cards.

My theory is that at some point there will be a set based around one
of these keywords. For example, a set where the government decides to
move against the Camarilla; this could introduce new Government cards
and effects that refer to them. A set based around the rise of the
Inconnu could be great. But what the hell does "Transient" mean? Very
mysterious. Maybe they are just red herrings, and we will never have
cards that refer to these keywords :)

Messages.Author: Amenophobis
Messages.Body:

There are two other new keywords in the new HttB set:
Moon Sigil (or New Moon Sigil?)
Nod Fragment

Now I think that new keywords are good to have because other cards can
key in on them. But, those 2 new keywords happen to have no other
cards referencing to them.
What purpose does it have to categorize Shaal Fragment as "Nod
Fragment"? (Similar question for the Sigil keyword.)
Right now it seems that the game gets cluttered with unwarranted
keywords. Do we really need keywords which are only repeated on 1
card?
Wouldn't it have more purpose that *if* a keyword is introduced, it
has some meaning, too? I mean, the Aim-cards are a good example of a
new keyword successfully implemented. Sigil would be fine if there
were at least 2 of those types. I know that it's possible to print
future Sigils, but why miss the opportunity in this set? This way it
adds unnecessary complexity (which some players would like to avoid I
gather from various web-sources).
And what about the "Nod fragment"?
Does this make sense to you?

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
"Amenophobis" <preac...@gmx.at> wrote in message
news:67e68b82-e44a-45e0...@d2g2000yqa.googlegroups.com...

> > > And what about the "Nod fragment"?

> > printed), like werewolf, grapple, electronic, etc.?
>
> Did I say that? Adding keywords where necessary is fine.

You didn't say that. Others (like me) don't like it. Every time a
card is given errata or reprinted with something significant added,
changed, or removed in a different set (effectively causing the old
versions of a card to have the equivalent of errata) it causes
confusion that hurts the game. People play old versions of the card
and forget or never know they've been changed. New players buy older
cards, put them in decks, and don't realize until later that they
don't do exactly what it says on the card.

I think sometimes errata or reprinting with changes is better than
alternative ways of handling a bad situation that arises (when a
card's text as printed turns out to cause a worse problem in the game
than the errata would) so it should be a tool that card designers are
free use. But it should be avoided when not strictly necessary.
Scott is right: printing keywords that don't seem to do anything
for the moment is far more benign than changing a card after the
fact. I'm really confused why you think non-functional keywords
cause a problem.

Fred

I think it's good for the developers to think ahead.

Other posters have already given anecdotes about allies. Other
examples include Abomination (introduced in Final Nights, far before
their official debut as crypt cards in KMW). Final Nights also
introduced Week of Nightmares and Tajdid, which would probably be more
appropriate as Events nowadays (but there was no realistic way they
could have predicted what would come in Gehenna).

Key words are useful for flavor and thematic reasons. And they make it
simpler when certain cornercase cards have cornercase specials.
Instead of having to list a comprehensive and exhaustive list of cards
(which may need to be errata'ed as new cards are printed), sorting
such cards into a keyword makes things far more elegant.

For example, look at Bindusara, Historian of the Kindred, who can
retrieve: Arcane Library, Elder Library or Fragment of the Book of
Nod.

If we were to do this again, it might make sense to have the Fragment
be a "Nod Fragment," and Arcane/Elder Library have the "Library"
keyword, so that Bindusara could simply retrieve Libraries and Nod
Fragments.

Suppose Smite simply said "IR Goggles, Laptop Computer, or Phased
Motion Detector" (instead of an Electronic keyword). Then things get
complicated when Camera Phone and Light Intensifying Goggles are
printed. They wouldn't be on the list of cards, so you'd have to
either change Smite, or deal with some logical inconsistencies. Thus,
the Electronic keyword simplifies the process (even though it's only
for a single card - Smite).
